bull.b: Fast Track designation gives Perspective closer FDA interaction while advancing PSV359 in a cancer area with limited treatment options. It can help focus development planning and supports the strategic relevance of the company’s broader 212Pb radiopharmaceutical platform.

A multi-program 212Pb pipeline combined with integrated, IP-protected infrastructure creates a potentially differentiated position across the radiopharmaceutical value chain. Regional production and direct-to-hospital delivery may support reliable fulfillment as clinical programs advance.

Very low leverage reduces financial distress risk and preserves flexibility while Perspective funds clinical development. Growth in equity also supports the asset base, giving the company more capacity to pursue milestones without relying primarily on debt financing.

bear.b: Revenue remains extremely small and volatile relative to the company’s cost base, while persistent operating and net losses show that commercial scale has not yet been established. This weak earnings foundation limits internally generated funding and keeps execution dependent on pipeline progress.

Heavy and persistent cash outflows indicate that research, development, and operating needs are consuming liquidity before profitability is reached. Continued burn can require additional funding over time and may constrain the pace or scope of future clinical and manufacturing investment.

Increasing R&D expense alongside a wider net loss raises the financial burden of advancing the pipeline before any product revenue is established. Although investment may support clinical progress, it also increases near-term funding needs and prolongs exposure to unprofitable operations.
